props.title: Hidden Wealth
lines: Wealth is what you do not see: the cars not bought, the upgrades declined.
Spending is the visible part. The unseen pile is the whole point.

rows.v: Wealth is financial assets that have not yet been converted into stuff.
Rich is current income. Wealth is unspent income. A high salary with a high burn rate can be poor in options.
We study visible spending and copy it. We cannot study the neighbor's brokerage lot.
The U.S. uses about 60% less energy per dollar of G.D.P. than it did decades ago — efficiency is invisible like savings.
The world is filled with people who look rich and are one paycheck from tight. Judge unseen reserves, not chrome.

props.title: Why we copy the wrong neighbor

left.name: What is visible
lines: Cars, watches, additions, vacations posted online.
That spending is the opposite of wealth. It is wealth converted into stuff.

right.name: What is hidden
lines: Brokerage lots, paid-off houses, unused credit lines, a job you can quit.
You cannot screenshot someone else's savings rate. So you copy their burn rate instead.
The 60% drop in energy per dollar of G.D.P. is the same shape: the win is the waste you do not see.

props.title: Judge reserves, not chrome
items: When you see a nice lifestyle, remember you are seeing the expense, not the net worth.
The most valuable assets do not photograph well. That is the point.
Building wealth is often the art of looking poorer than you are, on purpose.

props.title: Copy the reserve, not the burn
items: What you can see is the expense. What you cannot see is the net worth.
Savings rates do not screenshot well. That is why people copy lifestyles instead.
Looking poorer than you are can be a strategy, not a failure of taste.
Judge the iceberg. The boat is just the part that photographs.
